note: A writer's account of a haunted tour of the street. Fragments read: at Glessner House a 'pleasant presence', and a cold that sometimes fills a warm room; at the Kimball house shutters that shake when the air is still and Evalyne Kimball, late in life, 'entertaining empty rooms she thought were full of visitors'; at the Field Jr. house, new owners who reportedly had an exorcism, a spirit that 'sours the air around it'. The writer declines to repeat the 1812 battle-ground sightings.
